MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  November 3, 2025

Chair Legaspi called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll call were
Chair LeGaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins,
Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez and Commissioner Greenidge. Also, present was Rita Ruiz,
Interim Director, Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Vice Chair Rosoff Commissioner Hoskins motioned for the approval of the minutes of the
Public Safety Commission Meeting minutes that was held on October 6, 2025.
Commissioner

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair Legaspi Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner  Apodaca,
  Commissioner Hoskins, and Commissioner Greenidge
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

H.O.P.E. Team Presentation

Interim Director Rita Ruiz introduced Public Safety Sergeant Jozeph Ruelas, who
provided an update on the H.O.P.E. Team. Sergeant Ruelas has been with Public Safety
for seven years, serving one year as a part-time sergeant before being promoted to full-
time sergeant, a role he has now held for one year. His previous assignments include
Training Officer, Shift Lead, and various other positions throughout the department.

Sergeant Ruelas shared that he joined the H.O.P.E. Team three months ago and noted
that it has been his favorite assignment so far. He also acknowledged the strong
leadership previously provided by Sergeants Warren and Garcia.

H.O.P.E. Mission & Goals

  •  Improve the quality of life for people experiencing homelessness by connecting
  them with partner organizations.
  •  Enhance public safety through homeless-focused operations.
  •  Reduce the number of unhoused individuals through ongoing partnerships.
  •  Support long-term transition out of homelessness.
 Program Approach

Sergeant Ruelas reported that the team focuses on outreach, collaboration, and
advocacy. Their approach includes connecting individuals to housing, substance-abuse
programs, and mental-health services. Many individuals encountered are first-time
offenders or unfamiliar with certain laws, making education a key component.

The team works closely with internal departments and external agencies—including
regional partners in Los Angeles, San Pedro, and Whittier—to coordinate outreach and
connect individuals with resources. Long-term follow-up is a priority to help prevent
relapses and support individuals once they are placed in shelters or transitional housing.
We would also like to recognize our Social Services Team for managing all onboarding
and paperwork, which is extremely time-consuming and requires meticulous attention to
detail.

Examples of Outreach

  •  An individual recognized the HOPE Team from the city website and approached
  officers requesting assistance; services were coordinated with support from LASD
  partners.

  •  Two long-term transients in the Firestone/Studebaker area were contacted; one
  was successfully reunited with family, and the other sought help after speaking
  with a recently housed peer.

These examples highlight the impact of visible success stories and the importance of
sustained engagement.

Data & Operations (January–September 2025)

Clean-ups: 676

Referrals: 203

Reports/Resources: 372

Recent notable operation included a Halloween cleanup with Union Pacific Railroad,
during which 11 individuals were contacted and seven encampments addressed. Data
continues to guide operations, area prioritization, and resource deployment.

Community Feedback

Residents report:

  •  Noticeable decreases in homelessness in key areas.
  •  Improved overall cleanliness compared to surrounding cities.
   •  Appreciation for the team’s consistency, presence, and proactive engagement.
  •  Community members recognize the team’s efforts in preventing large
  encampments, maintaining safer public spaces, and providing support-oriented
  interactions.

STAFF COMMENTS

Interim Director Rita Ruiz reported The Public Safety Mission and Vision Survey is
being finalized for presentation to City Council. Printed copies are available for those
who haven’t completed them online. The survey is simple, yes/no answers with initials
and can also be done digitally. Feedback will be collected and processed to finalize the
Commission’s mission and vision.

Vision Statement:

The Public Safety Commission is dedicated to fostering a safe, informed, and engaged
community by partnering with residents, City leaders, and Public Safety Officers. The
Commission is committed to transparency, ethical conduct, and professional
representation.

Mission Statement:

  •  Educate and involve residents in understanding Public Safety and the Los
  Angeles Sheriff’s Department.
  •  Support law enforcement and City initiatives through participation in events,
  outreach programs, and public engagement.
  •  Uphold accountability and professionalism through consistent attendance, ethical
  training, and visible representation at City meetings and events.
  •  Serve with dedication, loyalty, and honesty to strengthen trust between the City,
  Public Safety personnel, and the community.
  •  Strive to be visible, approachable, and committed partners in ensuring the well-
  being of Norwalk and its residents.

Department Monthly Update:

Mrs. Lomas reviewed the 2025 Monthly Calendar and highlighted recent activities. She
noted that the City of Norwalk Public Safety Commission, together with the Community
Promotion Commission, hosted the First Responders Luncheon at the Norwalk Arts and
Sports Complex, with participation from the Norwalk Sheriff’s Station, CHP, and LA
County Fire.

She reported that Officers Warren, Arce, and Swanson hosted a Neighborhood Watch
meeting at Village Baptist Church to address quality-of-life concerns in Corner 2.
Additionally, Officers Rosas and Guerrero attended a clergy meeting at New Creation
Church, offering local religious leaders the opportunity to hear updates from Public Safety
officers and the Social Services Superintendent.
 Officers Carranza and Arce did a pedestrian safety presentation at the Norwalk Senior
Center. Officer Carranza, along with McGruff the Crime Dog and Public Safety Cadets,
also participated in this year’s Arturo Sanchez Halloween Parade.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS
Chair Legaspi thanked the HOPE Team for their great work and noted a noticeable
decrease in homelessness numbers following the recent count.

Commissioner Greenidge-Green shared that she was pleasantly surprised to see the
HOPE Team working early on a Saturday morning. Around 7:30 a.m., she observed an
unhoused female near miscellaneous dumped items and graffiti behind a business and
thanked both the HOPE Team and the Graffiti Crew for their prompt cleanup efforts.

She also inquired about the status of faded signage in her area, noting that worn stop
signs, street-sweeping signs, and parking signs pose safety concerns. Interim Director
Rita informed the Commission that the concern has been entered into the Public Services
work order system. She will follow up on the status and report back.

Commissioner Apodaca requested that the Commission discuss electric bikes at an
upcoming meeting. She noted increasing concerns from residents regarding e-bikes
being ridden on sidewalks, often by underage riders without helmets and sometimes
carrying multiple passengers. She asked for clarification on current rules and regulations.

Before moving to questions, Commissioner Apodaca also acknowledged the strong field
work being done by staff. She noted that consistent monitoring and engagement keep
areas from becoming stagnant, prevent trash accumulation, and make a visible difference
in the community. She thanked staff for their hard work and for the well-prepared
presentation.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:31 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
